description:
Externalize provider implementations as separate binaries with a standardized stdio contract, mirroring the tool-binary pattern from ARCH §3.3. Motivation: lets external contributors (corporate users with custom SSO/auth) ship a provider adapter without touching core code.

=== Scope (spec only; no code changes) ===
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: amend §4 (Providers, Auth, Models). Introduce the term 'provider adapter' for the binary; keep the existing (endpoint, auth) sense of 'provider'. Define the adapter contract: discovery, subcommands (describe, complete), stdin payload, stdout JSON/JSONL, error protocol, cancellation (SIGTERM), auth via env vars, schema versioning. Extend §3.1 (disk-as-bus) and §3.2 (components) to list the adapter as an external process invoked per model call.
- docs/PRINCIPLES.md: add or extend a principle covering 'externalized components via stdio' — this is now the pattern for both tools and providers, not a tool-only thing.
- docs/TAXONOMY.md: add 'provider adapter' as a term of art distinct from 'provider'. Note this is a lernie-specific coinage; the taxonomy already flags 'provider' as overloaded (§2).
- README.md: small note under 'Conversation repos' or a new 'Providers' section if helpful.

=== Out of scope (follow-up task) ===
- Refactoring the existing Anthropic messages-API client (commit 740f61a, bl-9600) into an adapter binary.
- Adapter discovery implementation (PATH lookup, config plumbing).
- Streaming event bus plumbing in the harness.

=== Interaction with bl-e048 ===
bl-e048 (prompt subcommand) builds on the current in-process Anthropic client. Two paths forward — user's call:
  (a) proceed with bl-e048 as written, refactor to the adapter contract in a separate task afterward;
  (b) pause bl-e048 until the adapter refactor lands.
Either is fine; the amendment itself doesn't block either choice.

=== Contract summary (full text lands in ARCH §4) ===

Discovery: binary named 'lernie-provider-<name>' on PATH, overridable via providers.yaml 'adapter:' key.

Subcommands:
  describe  — no stdin; stdout: single JSON {name, schema_version, capabilities, models[], auth_env[]}.
  complete  — stdin: JSON request (Anthropic messages-API shape; other adapters translate internally).
              stdout: one JSON response object (non-streaming) OR JSONL event stream (streaming).
              Event types model block-oriented content: message_start, content_block_start/stop, text_delta, tool_use_delta, message_stop with usage + api_calls.

Errors:
  Terminal event (streaming) or top-level object (non-streaming): {type:'error', kind:'retryable'|'fatal', http_status, message, retry_after_seconds}.
  Adapter owns retry loops for transient errors. Harness treats one 'complete' call as one model call.
  Exit code 0 = normal (including 'type: error' events). Non-zero = adapter crashed.

Cancellation: SIGTERM → drop in-flight HTTP, flush partial state, exit ≤ 5s. SIGKILL after.

Auth: env vars only, forwarded by name from describe.auth_env. Custom SSO flows live inside the adapter (keyring, aws-sso, Okta CLI, etc.); harness is uninvolved.

Schema versioning: describe.schema_version is an integer. Harness rejects unknown major versions at load.

=== Done-when ===
Amendment lands in ARCH/PRINCIPLES/TAXONOMY/README. cargo test, tarpaulin, clippy still green. Alignment gate checks the three spec docs are mutually consistent (no dangling references to 'provider' meaning two things, no principle contradicting the spec, taxonomy defines every new term used).
title: Spec amendment: provider adapter contract
